name: adam_step
summary: Adam update (F32) with BC1/BC2 scalars. Supports in-place P/M/V, forbids other aliasing. If Pout!=P, launcher copies P->Pout before update to keep kernel logic safe.
contract: Inputs (6): P, G, M, V, BC1, BC2
- Pout matches P shape, Mout matches M, Vout matches V
- Forbidden: any cross-alias between {P,M,V} groups (e.g., P==M, M==V, etc.)
- Forbidden: if not in-place, outputs aliasing other buffers
abi: Payload (16 bytes): float32 lr, beta1, beta2, eps (little-endian).
Defaults if schema_id==0 or invalid: lr=1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8.
NOTE: variant expected_attr_schema_id == 'ADAM' so exec should send schema_id='ADAM' for matching.
notes: Kernel: adam_step_f32_kernel_v2 grid-stride loop, threads=256, blocks=ceil(n/256) capped 65535.
BC1/BC2 are device scalar pointers; kernel reads bc1[0], bc2[0] (fallback 1.0 if null).
Launcher ensures OOP safety: if Pout!=P, do cudaMemcpyAsync(P -> Pout) before kernel, then kernel uses Pout = Pout - lr*(...).
Potential perf focus: bandwidth vs math (sqrtf). Consider fast-math, vectorization, fuse BC scalars into attrs, reduce loads.

variants.name: adam_step_f32_v2
supported: P,G,M,V same shape; outputs match respective shapes
alias policy enforced: only per-buffer in-place allowed; G cannot alias anything
variants.notes: Launcher performs P->Pout copy if OOP. Kernel updates M/V then Pout.

experiments.title: OOP safety via P->Pout memcpy
experiments.change: If Pout!=P, launcher copies P to Pout before kernel. Kernel always updates Pout in-place style.
experiments.why: Kernel uses 'Pout = Pout - ...' update. Without copy, OOP would read garbage/uninitialized Pout.
experiments.hypothesis: In-place path fastest; OOP adds memcpy cost proportional to n*sizeof(float).
experiments.proof: nsys timeline: memcpy + kernel; compare latency. Validate numerics vs reference.
experiments.next: If OOP common, consider kernel reading P separately (P pointer) to avoid memcpy; or fuse memcpy into kernel (load P and write Pout).

experiments.title: Math path: sqrtf + eps
experiments.change: Baseline uses sqrtf(v_hat) + eps; examine fast-math / rsqrt approximations.
experiments.why: sqrtf can be expensive; could trade precision for speed in training loops.
experiments.hypothesis: fast-math or rsqrt improves latency slightly on large n; verify stability/accuracy.
experiments.proof: ncu: instruction mix (sqrt), achieved occupancy, dram throughput. Compare loss stability in small training loop.
experiments.next: Try __frsqrt_rn + refinement; test effect with BC and eps.

measurements.notes: For optimizer kernels, report latency + effective GB/s. TFLOP/s optional.
